scene_state_transition_model.statement: The source-defined playing world has an 800-by-600 coordinate extent and initializes a player, sentence-word prisoners, an empty trail, an empty monster array, and a portal at the cited positions.

While playing, the advance function updates player movement, prisoners, trail, monsters, collisions, and victory checking in the cited order; player input is diagonal-normalized, speed- and dt-scaled, and clamped inside the rectangular world boundary.
Prisoner contact is radius-based: the next ordered word is appended to the trail, while an out-of-order contact makes the prisoner flee for 1500 ms and rescatteres and resets the collected trail.
Monster-trail contact rescatteres the affected trail suffix and grants invulnerability; player-monster contact clears a nonempty trail or decrements lives and enters defeat at zero lives.

The source-defined victory state requires portal contact and a trail whose length equals the sentence word count; the component then awards XP and correct-word totals, calls advanceToNextLevel, and installs the returned next state.
The next-level reset increments level, creates a new sentence and prisoner set, appends one monster, and resets trail, target index, and player position for playing.
The source-defined start branch renders the start screen; its callback resets the game, sets phase to playing, and enters fullscreen.

The component obtains directional input and a virtual-input setter, maintains camera x/y/scale, follows and clamps the camera to the player, declares a virtual directional pad, and defines the cited responsive play-container classes.

The source references four gameplay asset paths and the page fetches locale-specific sentences before passing them to the game; these are source references only, not load, browser, or route-execution observations.

The indicator calculation excludes collected or fleeing prisoners, projects remaining positions through camera scale and offset, and creates an edge-positioned indicator for positions outside the viewport.

mechanics_learning_model.statement: The source-defined learning interaction presents sentence words as ordered prisoners: collecting the next word appends it to the trail, while wrong-order contact triggers flee, rescatter, and reset consequences.
Completion is source-gated by collecting every sentence word before portal contact; the resulting victory path awards XP and correct-word totals and hands off to a reset next level.
Monster contact supplies the source-defined hazard loop: trail interaction rescatteres a suffix and grants invulnerability, while contact without a trail costs a life and can defeat.

The component obtains directional input and a virtual-input setter, and renders VirtualDPad with that setter; these are source-level integration and component-wiring propositions, not proof of native execution.
The start-screen label declares Arrows / WASD as controls; keyboard event binding, trusted native execution, and browser learning behavior remain unknown.
